fields.explore_cta: Build My Food Bank Application Form
fields.features_heading: What Happens After a Household Applies
fields.features_subheading: A printed sheet ends at the signature line. These six pieces handle what intake volunteers now track on clipboards.
fields.feature_1:
Household size counted per member

Add each member with an age band, or let the applicant enter one total. The record stores the household size your state's TEFAP paperwork asks for and feeds the monthly count.
fields.feature_2:
Income declared against your state's limit

Show the limit your state agency sets for each household size. The applicant ticks a statement, and the basis for eligibility is saved with the date and the volunteer's name.
fields.feature_3:
Paper applications read into the records

Scan the sheets from a mobile distribution or a walk-in morning. Emergent reads each one into the same fields, and a household size it cannot read goes to a staff member to confirm.
fields.feature_4:
Each pantry sees its own households

Give every partner pantry a login that shows only the households routed to it. Food bank staff see the whole network, while volunteers at the table see names and pickup slots.
fields.feature_5:
Consent asked before any referral

Ask whether the household agrees to be referred to SNAP or WIC outreach. A record without that consent stays on the pantry's own list and never goes to either program's staff.
fields.feature_6:
Your code, on a server you choose

Export the full code to the food bank's GitHub repository. A volunteer developer can host it wherever the board decides, and client records stay in a database the food bank owns.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Jobs a Food Bank Application Does
fields.tab_content_1:
Five people, one income statement, no ID requested

Harbor Valley Food Bank keeps its client application to what the TEFAP record needs. Claire Novak ticked the statement that her household's income is at or below the state's limit. The record saved her name, a household size of 5 and the basis "Income, self-declared". The form never asked her for an ID.
fields.tab_content_2:
Eastside sees only the households from ZIP 40212

Families in Harbor Valley's network type a ZIP code first. The ZIP code picks the partner pantry that receives the application, never whether the household qualifies. ZIP 40212 belongs to Eastside Community Pantry. Coordinator Dana Okafor sees the 186 households routed there and none from other pantries.
fields.tab_content_3:
Saturday fills slot by slot, with a Friday reminder

Saturday at Lincoln Street Pantry runs on booked pickup times. The application ends with a choice of 15-minute slots, six households each, 72 places in all. This week 64 are booked and 8 are open. Each booked household gets an email on Friday with its slot time.
fields.tab_content_4:
What three sites add up to in September

September closes with the figure the food bank reports to its state agency: people served per distribution site. Emergent adds up the household sizes of each family served that month. Eastside served 1,140 people and Lincoln Street 860. With the mobile pantry's 412, the total is 2,412, and Marcus Hale exports the table.

fields.howto_title: How to Build a Food Bank Application Form
fields.howto_description: Start from your state agency's criteria. The form follows them.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pull up your state's TEFAP criteria
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Keep the questions to what you use
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Map partner pantries to ZIP codes
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Set pickup slots for each site
fields.howto_step_1_des: Find the eligibility criteria and income chart your state agency publishes for TEFAP. Note the limit for each household size and the ways a household may show it qualifies. Those details become the income statement and the basis field on every record.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask only for the name of the person collecting food, the number of people at home and the basis for eligibility. Leave the street address optional and skip ID. Every extra question adds time at the intake table and data you then have to protect.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write down every partner pantry, the ZIP codes it serves and its distribution days. Where two pantries share a ZIP code, offer both. The map decides only where an application goes. A household from any ZIP code still reaches a pantry.
fields.howto_step_4_des: List each site's distribution hours, the slot length and how many households fit in one slot. A three-hour Saturday in 15-minute slots of six gives 72 places. Decide when reminders go out and what a household sees once a day is full.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste the criteria, the ZIP map and the slot rules into one prompt. Emergent builds the application, the client database, a view for each partner pantry and the monthly count. Ask for a change in plain words, and the form and records update together.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Add the languages your clients read
fields.howto_step_6_des: Write the questions in each language your clients use, such as English and Spanish, and ask Emergent for every version. All of them save into the same fields. A household size entered in Spanish counts the same as one entered in English.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Run a test with two volunteers
fields.howto_step_7_des: Ask two volunteers to apply as one family from a ZIP code you know and book a Saturday slot. Check that the right pantry gets the record, the open places drop by one and the reminder is queued. Then post the link on your website.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is individual food banks' own client applications and intake PDFs, a few volunteer and food drive sheets, and one Jotform template. Each one stops at the filled-in page. This page is written for the food bank or pantry office that receives those applications: what the form records for USDA Foods under TEFAP, how a ZIP code sends a household to the partner pantry that serves it, how pickup slots fill, and how household sizes become the monthly count of people served. It gives applicants no advice on benefits; the state agency's own criteria decide eligibility.

Lincoln Street Pantry opens 72 Saturday pickup places in 15-minute slots of six, 64 are booked, and each booked household gets an email reminder on Friday.

claims_to_source: Each state agency sets uniform statewide criteria for household eligibility for TEFAP USDA Foods, with a maximum income threshold at or between 185 and 300 percent of the federal poverty guidelines
The household must live in the area the state agency serves when it applies, and length of residency, an address or identification documents cannot be used as eligibility criteria
Each distribution site records the name of the household member receiving USDA Foods, the number of people in the household and the basis for eligibility
TEFAP records are kept for 3 years from the close of the federal fiscal year they pertain to
Applicant information may be used or disclosed only to people directly connected with running the program, and with the participant's consent it may be shared with other health or welfare programs
FNS allows households to self-declare income, and the state agency decides whether to require verification
The TEFAP eligibility rules for address, ID and the income threshold changed under a final rule published October 31, 2024, effective December 30, 2024
State agencies report to FNS the total number of persons served by each distribution site, from the household sizes distribution sites collect
